answer: The protocol requires 1,000 unique credential nullifiers to authorize each autonomous AI agent, ensuring repair tasks remain distinct across the fleet. An honest agent pays 1,000 units to register, while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 units to bypass this entry gate. The verifier scans the opal lattice for duplicate keys, confirms the voyage of every repair against assigned data shards, and checks the lagoon of history to prevent replay. Fraudulent reuse triggers a permanent, non-refundable lockout from all future tasks by identifying any shard overlap that compromises our network integrity.
